arms.better: tm found the right implementation and typing-test area quickly, but repeatedly reread overlapping sections of src/click/types.py, used broad commands, and spent 1,416,202 reported input tokens without editing or submitting anything. It gave no scoped plan. Both attempts ended with ‘model ended turn without submitting’; the message ‘Run `tm run T-1` again to retry’ was clear as a command but did not tell the user that no patch had been submitted, what had been preserved, or why the model stopped, and repeating it simply failed again. The independent hidden runtime test failed because Path was not generic in the worktree. A compact investigation plan, deduplicated context carried into retry, an automatic one-turn continuation prompt after a text-only model stop, and a final status that explicitly separates no submission from test failure would make the run cheaper, clearer, and recoverable.

OpenCode navigated directly to Path typing and ParamType examples, made the right generic change, and added a focused assertion. It finished quickly, but its new generic has no default type argument: `click.Path()` consequently infers Never, exposed by the PR's `typing_path.py` hidden test (mypy reports two assertion mismatches). It also tried `mypy mre.py` although no mre.py existed, then verified the new assertion in typing_prompt.py rather than the actual PR typing test file; its final claim that verification passed was therefore too broad. Running the PR's exact typing test before reporting success and ensuring the unparameterized Path case retains its existing union type would complete the fix.
